lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Humans are restless, adaptable, and ambitious, making much of their brief lives and finding strength in one another.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Humans are everywhere, and everywhere they are different. No other people spreads so far, argues so loudly, or reinvents itself so often. A human border town can change its laws, its faith, and its skyline inside a single generation; an elf who naps through a decade returns to find the maps redrawn. What humans lack in long memory they repay in momentum, and the other peoples watch them with a mix of admiration and alarm.

That restlessness is personal as much as cultural. A human feels the shortness of their years and answers it with ambition: one more field cleared, one more deal struck, one more mountain nobody sensible would climb. At their best, humans bind strangers into companies and companies into causes. At their worst, they burn through places, promises, and people the way they burn through years.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who can come from anywhere, get along with anyone, and refuse to stay in any lane, you should play a human.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
• Chase a goal so hard that rest starts to feel like theft.
• Collect skills, contacts, and causes the way others collect coins.
• Assume any problem can be solved if you just find the right people for it.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
• Envy how quickly you learn, adapt, and move on.
• Wonder what you are running from, or racing toward.
• Trust your knack for finding common ground, even between old enemies.

lore.label: Physical Description (at a glance)
lore.text: Humans are middling in most measures and wildly varied in all of them. They stand roughly five to six and a half feet tall, in every build from wiry to broad, with skin, hair, and eyes spanning every shade their homelands offer. What marks a human crowd is not a shared look but a shared motion: quick eyes, busy hands, and clothing that borrows freely from every neighbor they have ever traded with.

lore.label: Physical Description (life cycle)
lore.text: Humans reach physical adulthood around 15 years and are usually granted a place at the adults' table by 18, though every town draws that line differently. A human who avoids war, plague, and their own ambition can expect sixty to ninety years, and a rare few see a century. Their short season is the quiet engine of their character; humans plant orchards whose shade they will never sit in, and they know it.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
Human society is less a single design than a permanent argument about what the design should be. Kingdoms, leagues, free towns, wandering companies: humans have tried them all, usually at the same time, usually within a week's ride of each other. Their gift is the joining of strangers. A human market will seat a dwarven smith beside an elven dyer and a gnomish clockmaker, and by closing time the three will share a ledger and a grudge against the harbormaster.

Because they invent themselves so freely, humans put enormous weight on names, oaths, and reputations, the few things that outlive them. A human's word, once given before witnesses, is a load-bearing wall; whole towns stand on webs of such promises. Breaking one is not just a sin but a kind of vandalism.

Humans honor their dead by continuing their projects. Workshops, farms, feuds, and half-built bridges pass from hand to hand like torches, and a human family can often recite what each generation added to the house even when they have forgotten the builders' faces.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text: Human belief runs hot and plural. One village keeps six shrines and hedges its bets at all of them; the next follows a single creed with terrifying focus. What is consistent is the human conviction that effort matters, that the world is unfinished, and that somebody, probably them, ought to get on with finishing it. Their prayers tend to be practical: strength for the harvest, luck for the crossing, courage for the morning.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
• Leave every place better than you found it.
• Keep your word once witnesses have heard it.
• Lift the newcomer; you were one once.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
• Waste a year owed to the people who raised you.
• Break a promise made before witnesses.
• Let fear of failing keep you from beginning.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Human given names vary widely between families and homelands. Many human surnames preserve an ancestor’s occupation, carrying the memory of a workshop, livelihood, or useful skill through generations. A family named Cooper might have stopped making barrels centuries ago, yet still treasure the name.

Common given names Alden, Bram, Cassia, Doran, Elsbeth, Garron, Hale, Imre, Joss, Lysa, Mara, Oren, Sera, Tavin, Wren, Ysolde.

Common surnames Baker, Carter, Cooper, Fletcher, Mason, Miller, Roper, Tanner, Turner, Weaver.

Example names Alden Cooper, Cassia Fletcher, Elsbeth Weaver, Garron Mason, Lysa Carter, Tavin Roper.

nodes.name: Humanity
nodes.effect:
You gain 8 Vigor per level. Your Speed is 6 feet. Your Size is Medium. You gain the Human trait.

Bonus to Aid. You gain a +1 Condition bonus on checks to Aid.
nodes.desc: Humans are restless, adaptable, and ambitious, making much of their brief lives and finding strength in one another.

nodes.name: Driven
nodes.effect: You gain a Calling Talent Point.
nodes.desc: Once you find your purpose, you pursue it with a determination that rarely lets you rest.

nodes.name: Quick Study
nodes.effect: You gain a Skill Talent Point.
nodes.desc: You have a knack for turning a little instruction into a useful new skill.

nodes.name: Stubborn Footing
nodes.effect: The first time each encounter you would be knocked prone, you are not.
nodes.desc: Even when a blow catches you off balance, sheer stubbornness keeps you on your feet.

nodes.name: Close Ranks
nodes.effect: While an ally is adjacent to you, both of you gain a +1 Situation bonus to Guard against Blows.
nodes.automation: bonus: +1, Situation, Guard, AGAINST(Blow), FOR(self+allies, 0ft), WHILE(allies>=1, 0ft)
nodes.desc: Shoulder to shoulder, you and your companions instinctively cover one another’s openings.

nodes.name: Torchbearer Human
nodes.effect: You gain the Rally Aura: The first time each round an ally within 15 feet who can see you defends against an Attack with the Fear trait, they gain a +1 Situation bonus to that Defense check.
nodes.automation:
aura: 15ft, allies, VISIBLE
bonus: +1, Situation, Defenses, FOR(allies, 15ft), FIRST(round)
nodes.desc: Others take heart from your presence, drawing courage from you and the example you set.

nodes.name: Steady the Line
nodes.effect:
You gain the Steady the Line ❶↺ Maneuver:
Trigger An adjacent ally would become Exposed.
Effect The adjacent ally does not become Exposed.
nodes.desc: You cut through the clash, steadying a companion’s defense before it can falter.

nodes.name: Versatile Human
nodes.effect: You gain 1 Opening Talent Point.
nodes.desc: Your interests lead in many directions, and you rarely let an opportunity to learn something new pass unexplored.

nodes.name: Jack of All Trades
nodes.effect: You gain a +1 Condition bonus to your Untrained checks.
nodes.desc: You have tried your hand at enough things to find a familiar thread in almost any task.

nodes.name: Ambusher Calling
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Stealth.

You gain the Sneak Attack Maneuver:
+1d6 precision damage vs. Off-Guard foes. Rises to +2d6 at Expert rank, +3d6 at Master, +4d6 at Legendary.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 8 Vigor and Training in Melee or Ranged.
nodes.desc: You stalk the edges of a fight, striking where attention falters and defenses leave an opening.

nodes.name: Surprise Attacker
nodes.effect: In the first round, foes that haven't acted yet are Wrong-Footed to you.
nodes.desc: You move while your enemies are still grasping the danger, catching them before they can gather themselves.

nodes.name: Opportunist ❶↺
nodes.effect:
Opportunist ❶↺

Trigger An ally Hits a creature within your reach.
Effect Strike that creature. It is Off-Guard to this Strike.
nodes.desc: An ally’s attack creates a moment of distraction, and you are ready to make it costly.

nodes.name: Twist the Blade
nodes.effect: Once per round, when your Sneak Attack damage applies to a Hit, the Zone it landed on becomes Exposed.
nodes.desc: You turn a precise strike into an opening in your enemy’s guard, leaving a vulnerable spot exposed.

nodes.name: Bleeding Wound
nodes.effect: When your Sneak Attack damage applies, the target also takes 1d4 persistent bleed damage. This rises to 1d6 at Expert rank, 1d8 at Master, and 1d10 at Legendary.
nodes.desc: You place your strikes where the bleeding is hardest to stop.

nodes.name: Unbalancing Blow
nodes.effect: Whenever your Strike is a critical hit and deals damage, the target is Wrong-Footed against your attacks until the end of the next round.
nodes.desc: A well-placed strike disrupts your enemy’s stance, leaving them scrambling to recover their guard.

nodes.name: Berserker Calling
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Athletics.

You gain the Rage action:
Rage ❶
Duration 10 rounds
You gain Temporary Vigor = level + Might, +2 melee damage, −1 Evade. While raging, you are Heedless.
Afterward, increase your Fatigued by 1 until you spend three actions to catch your breath.
You may end your Rage as a free action, increasing your Fatigued by 1 as though it had run its course.

Damage bonus rises to +4 melee damage at Expert rank, +6 at Master, +8 at Legendary.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 12 Vigor and Training in Melee or Ranged.

nodes.name: Sudden Charge ❷
nodes.effect:
You gain Sudden Charge:
Sudden Charge ❷
Move twice, then Quick Strike. Your Moves may provoke Intercepts as normal.

nodes.name: Thick Hide
nodes.effect: While you are Raging, every Zone on you has +1 Protection, including Zones with no armor at all. An Exposed Zone still counts as 0.

nodes.name: Blood in the Water
nodes.effect: When your Strike drops a creature while you are Raging, your Rage's remaining duration resets to 10 rounds.

nodes.name: Deaf to Pain
nodes.effect: You ignore the Fatigued condition while Raging, and when your Rage ends you need to spend only 1 action to catch your breath rather than 3.

nodes.name: Moment of Clarity ⓿
nodes.effect:
Frequency once per encounter
You push back your rage for a moment in order to think clearly. Until the end of this round, you lose your Heedless condition.

nodes.name: Bravo Calling
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Acrobatics.

You gain Panache whenever you critically succeed on a Strike, or when you successfully Feint or Demoralize.

You can hold one Panache at a time and you keep it until you spend it or the encounter ends (whichever happens first).

While you have Panache you gain a +1 Situation bonus to Evade and a +1-foot Situation bonus to your Speeds. At Expert rank, Speed bonus increases to 2 feet. At Master rank, your Evade bonus increases to +2. At Legendary rank, your Speed bonus increases to 3 feet.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 10 Vigor and Training in Melee or Ranged.

nodes.name: Finisher ❶
nodes.effect:
Spend your Panache and Strike, with the following effects:
Hit add 2d6 precision damage.
Graze add 1d6 precision damage.
You lose the Panache either way.

nodes.name: Opportune Parry ⓿↺
nodes.effect:
Trigger A creature's Strike against you is Stopped (a Graze or a Miss) while you have Panache.
Effect You take Control of the attacking weapon as though you had Parried, without spending an action.

nodes.name: Nimble Recovery
nodes.effect: While you have Panache, you may Recenter ⓿ once per round.

nodes.name: Bravo's Entrance
nodes.effect: You begin every encounter with Panache if you are not surprised.

nodes.name: Elegant Buckler
nodes.effect:
When you Raise a Shield ❶ to gain a Situation bonus to Guard from a buckler, increase the bonus from +1 to +2.
While you have a buckler raised, if a creature critically misses you with a Strike, you gain panache.

nodes.name: Extravagant Parry ❶
nodes.effect:
Requirements You're wielding one or more one-handed weapons
You gain a +1 Situation bonus to Guard until your next Opportunity, or a +2 Situation bonus if you have a free hand or are wielding a weapon with the parry trait. You lose this Situation bonus if you no longer meet this feat's requirement. If a creature misses you with a Strike while you have this bonus, you gain panache.

nodes.name: Hunter Calling
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Awareness.

(Concentrate) Choose one creature you can see. It is your prey until you Mark another or the encounter ends.

The first time each round that you Hit your prey, add 1d8 precision damage. You also always know roughly where your prey is while it is within 60 feet, even while it is Hidden or Undetected. The extra precision damage rises to 2d8 at Expert rank, 3d8 at Master, and 4d8 at Legendary.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 10 Vigor and Training in Melee or Ranged.

nodes.name: Running Mark
nodes.effect: You may Mark Prey as part of a Move rather than spending an action.

nodes.name: Read the Quarry
nodes.effect: The first time each encounter your prey attacks you, you learn if its Evade or Guard is higher.

nodes.name: Hobbling Strike
nodes.effect: When you Hit your prey with the first Strike of the round, its Speed is reduced by 2 feet until the end of the next round.

nodes.name: No Escape ❶↺
nodes.effect:
Trigger Your prey Moves away from you.
Effect Move up to your Speed toward it. This does not provoke Reactions from your prey.

nodes.name: Hunter's Aim ❷
nodes.effect: Make a Deliberate weapon Strike ❷ against your Marked Prey. On this Strike, you gain a +2 Situation bonus to the attack roll and ignore your prey's concealed condition and any lesser cover.

nodes.name: Weaponmaster Calling
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Athletics.

You gain the Weapon Familiarity Talent for free.

Choose one Weapon Group in which you are Familiar. When making attacks with weapons of that Group, treat your Weapons Proficiency Bonus as 2 higher. This does not actually increase your Proficiency Rank and does not satisfy Expert, Master, or Legendary prerequisites.

You may take the Reactive Strike Talent, even if you are not Expert in Melee. However, you may still only use Reactive Strike with weapons in which you are at least Expert Proficiency Rank.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 10 Vigor and Training in Melee or Ranged.

nodes.name: Hold the Line
nodes.effect: Your Intercept also triggers when a creature within your Reach uses any Motion Maneuver, whether or not it leaves your Reach.

nodes.name: Punishing Blow
nodes.effect: Your Intercept disrupts the triggering Maneuver on a Hit, not only a Critical Hit, if the Zone struck was Exposed.

nodes.name: Second Nature
nodes.effect: Your weapon specialization damage arrives one rank early with your Drilled group: +2 while Trained, +3 at Expert, +4 at Master, +5 at Legendary.

nodes.name: Hold Fast
nodes.effect: When one of your Strikes is Stopped and would Expose you, you may take 1 Vigor damage per level and Expose nothing instead.

nodes.name: Spellshaping
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Guile. Once per round, when declaring a Cast you know, you may add ❶ to its action cost to apply one alteration: extend the spell’s range by 5 feet; or, for an area spell, move one affected 1-foot square to an adjacent square outside the area, keeping the final affected space contiguous and the number of affected squares unchanged. Declare the alteration and any Prepared area before the first action is spent. Spell damage, Damage Dice, Threat, and Delivery do not change.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 6 Vigor and Training in Elementalism, or Forceweaving, Vitalism, Mindweaving, or Spiritcraft.

NEEDS Expert/Master/Legendary increases.

nodes.name: Selective Pattern
nodes.effect: When using Spellshaping with a Cast that affects an area, you may instead choose one ally you can see to be unaffected by that casting. Declare the ally before results are rolled. The added ❶ cost still applies.

nodes.name: Far Reaching
nodes.effect: When Spellshaping increases range, increase it by 10 feet rather than 5 feet. This does not increase the radius or number of targets of an area spell.

nodes.name: Hidden Pattern
nodes.effect: When using Spellshaping, you may obscure the precise target or area indicated by your gestures from observers more than 6 feet away. Speech and magical manifestations remain perceptible; this does not make preparation itself invisible.

nodes.name: Lingering Form
nodes.effect: When using Spellshaping on a spell with a duration ending at your next Opportunity, you may instead extend it until the end of that Opportunity. The spell does not gain additional attacks or repeated damage from this extension, and cannot be extended again by this Talent.

nodes.name: Blood Price
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Athletics. Once per round when declaring a damaging Cast from a magical parent in which you are Trained, you may lose Vigor equal to 1 + that parent’s Damage Dice. You must have enough Vigor to remain at 1 or more after paying. This loss cannot be prevented, redirected to Temporary Vigor, or reduced by Protection or Resistance. If the Cast Hits, add the same amount as bonus damage to ONE creature Hit. Pay before the roll; a Graze or Miss does not refund it. This is Vigor loss, not an Attack or a Wound.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 8 Vigor and Training in Elementalism, or Forceweaving, Vitalism, Mindweaving, or Spiritcraft.

NEEDS Expert/Master/Legendary increases.

nodes.name: Crimson Focus
nodes.effect: Once per encounter, when a Wound would automatically abandon your Prepared Cast, you may lose 2 additional Vigor (remaining at 1 or more) to retain the preparation. You suffer the Wound and its normal effects.

nodes.name: Scar Ward ❶↺
nodes.effect: Trigger: You take damage from a Blast or Blight that you can perceive. Lose 2 Vigor (remaining at 1 or more); reduce that instance of incoming damage by 3 after other mitigation. Once per round. Vigor paid for this Talent is not reduced by its effect.

nodes.name: Sanguine Reach
nodes.effect: When you use Blood Price on a single-target Cast, you may increase that spell’s range by 5 feet instead of adding Blood Price bonus damage. The Vigor cost is still paid, and this choice is made when the Cast is declared.

nodes.name: Deeper Offering
nodes.effect: When declaring Blood Price, you may lose 2 additional Vigor to increase its bonus damage by 2 against its one chosen target on a Hit. You must remain at 1 or more Vigor after all costs. No additional damage applies on a Graze or Miss.

nodes.name: Death Echo
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Awareness. Once per round, when a living creature you can perceive within 15 feet takes a Wound or becomes Spent, you may capture a Death Echo (maximum one held; it fades at encounter end). Before rolling one of your own Strikes or damaging Casts, you may expend the Echo: if that Attack Hits, add +2 damage to one creature Hit. This cannot trigger from summoned manifestations or from your own voluntary Vigor loss.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 6 Vigor and Training in Elementalism, or Forceweaving, Vitalism, Mindweaving, or Spiritcraft.

NEEDS Expert/Master/Legendary increases.

nodes.name: Read the Veil
nodes.effect: As ❶, examine a creature you can Observe within 6 feet. Learn whether it is Spent, visibly Wounded, or dead; supernatural disguises may require a separate Awareness check at GM discretion. This reveals neither hidden exact Vigor nor unobserved causes of death.

nodes.name: Grave Pressure
nodes.effect: When you expend a Death Echo and Hit, you may instead reduce one affected target’s Speed by 1 foot until the end of its next Opportunity. No bonus damage is added by Death Echo when you choose this effect.

nodes.name: Borrowed Resolve ❶↺
nodes.effect: Trigger: An ally within 6 feet suffers damage that would reduce them to 0 Vigor. Expend your Death Echo to reduce that instance of damage by 2, possibly preventing them from becoming Spent. The ally must be able to perceive you; once per round.

nodes.name: Harvest the Fallen
nodes.effect: Once per encounter, as ❶, capture a Death Echo from a corpse within 3 feet that died within the past minute. No creature may supply more than one Echo in this way. This does not animate or control the corpse.

nodes.name: Call Manifestation ❷
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Awareness. Create one 1-foot manifestation in an unoccupied square within 6 feet; it lasts until encounter end, you are Unconscious, or it is dismissed. You may have only one. It has Speed 6 feet and no independent actions. Command ❶ on your Opportunity to make it either Move up to its Speed or Strike an adjacent creature (Zoned Blow, 1d4 damage, using the chosen parent’s attack bonus). It uses your Evade or Guard when attacked and vanishes on a Hit; Graze does not dismiss it. It cannot use Reactions, Bind, Intercept, provide Support, or inflict Wounds. It never rolls Damage Dice for its Strike. Its form is cosmetic unless a Talent specifies otherwise.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 6 Vigor and Training in Elementalism, or Forceweaving, Vitalism, Mindweaving, or Spiritcraft.

NEEDS Expert/Master/Legendary increases.

nodes.name: Long Leash
nodes.effect: You may summon your manifestation within 10 feet instead of 6 feet. You may Command it while it is within 30 feet of you; otherwise it remains in place until you come into range or dismiss it.

nodes.name: Fighting Together
nodes.effect: Once per round, when you use Command ❶ to have your manifestation Strike and it Hits, you may Step 1 foot as a free effect. This Step does not provoke an Intercept from the creature it struck.

nodes.name: Interposing Form ❶↺
nodes.effect: Trigger: You or an ally within 3 feet of your manifestation would take damage from a Zoned Attack. Dismiss the manifestation and reduce that instance of damage by 2 after Protection. This is physical interception, not Resistance. Once per round.

nodes.name: Hardened Manifestation
nodes.effect: The first Hit that would dismiss your manifestation each encounter instead leaves it active; the next Hit dismisses it. This has no effect on Critical Hits, which still dismiss it immediately.

nodes.name: Spellbound Edge ❶
nodes.effect:
You become Trained in Athletics. Requirements: Trained in Melee and one magical parent, and you know a damaging spell from that parent. Choose one damage type dealt by that spell. Your next Deliberate Melee Strike begun before the end of your next Opportunity may deal the chosen type instead of its usual type. It remains a Zoned Blow, uses Melee proficiency and weapon dice, and gains no spell Damage Dice or other spell effects.

If this is your first Calling, you also gain 8 Vigor and Training in Elementalism, or Forceweaving, Vitalism, Mindweaving, or Spiritcraft.

Special You must already be Trained in either Melee or Ranged (or, if you take this at character creation, you must use one become Trained in Melee or Ranged before the end of the character creation process.

NEEDS Expert/Master/Legendary increases.

nodes.name: Guarded Conduit
nodes.effect: While preparing a Focused or Committed Cast and wielding a melee weapon, gain +1 Situation to Guard against Blows. This does not permit Guard against Blasts and ends when preparation ends.

nodes.name: Flicker Step
nodes.effect: Once per round after a Melee Strike enhanced by Spellbound Edge Hits, you may Step 1 foot as a free effect without provoking an Intercept from the creature you struck.

nodes.name: Attuned Edge
nodes.effect: Spellbound Edge may also enhance a Committed Melee Strike if you begin preparing it before the end of your next Opportunity. The chosen damage type persists until that Prepared Strike resolves or is abandoned. It still adds no spell dice or riders.

nodes.name: Spellstrike ❹
nodes.effect: Requirements: Trained in Melee and one magical parent; know a damaging Cast from that parent. Declare a Prepared melee Attack against one target in Reach and choose one known damaging spell. On a Hit, deal normal Deliberate Melee Strike damage plus ONE base damage die from the spell, with both parts treated as a single Zoned Blow against the same Zone (Protection applies once). On a Graze, use Deliberate Strike Graze damage with no spell die. On a Critical Hit, double the weapon damage after Protection as for Deliberate Strike, then add one undoubled spell die. No other effects of the spell apply. Roll using Melee, not magical proficiency.

Archery.meta: Combat Style • Agility (bows and careful ranged attacks)
Archery.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Archery Training
nodes.effect:
You learn this fighting style. Use your Ranged Proficiency for its checks and Attacks unless a technique specifies another check. Each Talent here contributes to your Ranged rank. You gain the Draw a Bead ❶ action.

Draw a Bead ❶ Concentrate
Choose one creature you can Observe and can reach with your bow.
Until the end of your next Opportunity:
your next bow Strike against that creature gains a +1 Situation bonus to the attack;
ignore the weapon's Unwieldy penalty for that Strike;
if that Strike Grazes, you choose the Zone it lands on instead of the defender.

nodes.name: Clear the Line
nodes.effect: Your ranged attacks treat Lesser Cover as no Cover.

nodes.name: Close Shot
nodes.effect: Reduce the minimum distance of Unwieldy by 5 feet. If that would reduce it to 0, the weapon no longer has Unwieldy for you.

Armored Fighting.meta: Combat Style • Presence (the harness as a weapon)
Armored Fighting.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Armored Fighting Training
nodes.effect:
You learn this fighting style. Use your Melee Proficiency for its checks and Attacks unless a technique specifies another check. Each Talent here contributes to your Melee rank.

When determining whether your armor forms a complete harness for an Armored Fighting Talent, all four Zones must be armored in the required material. If you are Master, only three Zones must be armored in the required material.
nodes.desc: Knowing how to exploit armor as part of your fighting method.

nodes.name: Ironclad
nodes.effect: While wearing Full Plate, gain +1 Condition bonus Physical Guard against Shove, Trip, and Reposition.
nodes.desc: You're not harder to hit generally. You're harder to move.

nodes.name: Trust the Harness
nodes.effect: While wearing Full Plate, when you would choose an armored Zone for a Graze, you may choose the Torso even if another rule would normally require another Zone.

nodes.name: Lock Down ❶
nodes.effect:
You settle your weight into your Full Plate harness.
While in this Stance:
+1 Condition bonus to Physical Guard.
You cannot be forcibly moved more than 3 feet by a single effect unless it critically succeeds.
Your Speed is reduced by 1 foot.

nodes.name: Punishing Shove
nodes.effect: When you successfully Shove a creature, that creature takes an amount of bludgeoning damage equal to your Might modifier (or double that amount on a Critical Success). This damage increases by 2 when you become an expert in Armored Fighting, 6 when you become a master, and 12 when you become legendary.
nodes.desc: When you push a foe away, you put the entire force of your Full Plate harness into it.

nodes.name: Shoulder Check ❶
nodes.effect:
You hit a foe with your armor to throw them off balance. Make a fist Strike even if you don't have a hand free; if you're wielding a gauntlet or spiked gauntlet, you can make a Strike with one of those weapons instead. The Strike gains the following additional results:
Critical Success The target is Wrong-Footed for you until the end of the next round.
Success The target is Wrong-Footed for you against the next Attack you attempt against it before the end of your next Opportunity.
Critical Failure You are Wrong-Footed against melee attacks the target attempts against you until the end of the next round.

nodes.name: Flowing Defense ❶
nodes.effect:
Flowing Defense ❶ Stance
While wearing Full Mail:
when you Recenter, you may also Step;
-1 Condition Physical Guard versus Shove
retains mail's normal vulnerability to piercing

nodes.name: Supple Harness
nodes.effect: Your first Step each round ignores 1 point of Load Strain's effect on movement-related checks.

nodes.name: Roll With It ❶↺
nodes.effect: When you are Grazed while wearing Full Mail, you may Step after resolving the attack and damage.

nodes.name: Turn the Scales ❶↺
nodes.effect: When you would be Hit, shift the blow to another armored, non-Exposed Zone.

nodes.name: Layered Guard ❶
nodes.effect:
Layered Guard ❶ Stance
While wearing Full Scale:
the first time each round a Zone becomes Exposed, another Zone of your choice gains +1 Protection until your next Opportunity.

nodes.name: Loose Guard
nodes.effect: While all four Zones are Padded or Leather and your Load Strain is 0, Recenter lets you Step as part of the action.

nodes.name: Light on Your Feet ❶
nodes.effect:
Light on Your Feet ❶ Stance
While in light armor:
+1 Condition Physical Evade;
After a creature Misses you, Step once per round;
Cannot be used if Load Strain exceeds 0.

Brawling.meta: Combat Style • Might (fists, feet, tusks, headbutts)
Brawling.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Brawling Training
nodes.effect:
You learn this fighting style. Use your Melee Proficiency for its checks and Attacks unless a technique specifies another check. Each Talent here contributes to your Melee rank. Every talent here requires this. You gain the Clinch action.

Clinch ❶ Stance While you are in this stance, a bare hand counts as a rigid implement: you may Parry, Bind, and Gain Control with it, and a creature whose weapon or limb you Control with a bare hand is also Grabbed. At Master rank, a creature you have Grabbed cannot Recenter.

nodes.name: Iron Fists
nodes.effect: Your unarmed strikes deal 1d6 and count as weapons (lethal by default, your choice).

nodes.name: Snagging Grip ❶
nodes.effect: Strike with a free hand; on a hit, the target is Off-Guard until your next Opportunity.

nodes.name: Crushing Grab

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Serrovanians build trust through witnessed promises, careful records, and the conviction that a person should answer for their word.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Serrovane is a lowland order-state of cultivated fields, raised roads, and towns gathered around registry halls. Its ledgers are kept in triplicate, its agreements carry witnesses, and its disputes follow forms that everyone is expected to respect. A promise spoken casually may be forgotten. A promise entered into the record becomes something other people can build their lives upon.

People of many ancestries belong to this order. An elven witness, a dwarven magistrate, and a human challenger may disagree bitterly while trusting the same record. Serrovanians learn how to state a grievance, acknowledge an obligation, and offer a concession without surrendering their standing. They can be formidable negotiators: they know exactly what they have promised, and they expect you to know the same.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who takes promises seriously, understands the power of public reputation, and can turn a few carefully chosen words into a lasting obligation, choose Serrovane.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
• Ask who witnessed an agreement before asking whether it was a good one.
• Carry copies of important promises, judgments, or introductions among your belongings.
• Insist on settling the terms of a contest before anyone draws a weapon.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
• Trust you to remember an obligation long after everyone else has forgotten it.
• Find your careful questions reassuring, exhausting, or faintly threatening.
• Worry that an innocent remark might become a commitment in your hearing.

lore.label: Dress and Bearing
lore.text:
Serrovanian clothing favors orderly layers, durable fabrics, and visible signs of affiliation. Household colors, office badges, and witness cords help others recognize whom a person represents. Garments vary with ancestry, occupation, and means, but people generally take care that closures are secure and identifying marks remain legible.

Formal bearing matters as much as fine clothing. Standing to acknowledge a witness, leaving another speaker room to finish, and presenting a document with clean hands all communicate respect.

lore.label: Upbringing and Milestones
lore.text:
Children learn promises through ordinary responsibilities: returning borrowed tools, delivering messages accurately, and admitting when a task remains unfinished. Many households preserve a young person’s first independently witnessed obligation.

Public responsibility follows demonstrated judgment, with its timing shaped by ancestry and family custom. Taking an office, joining a household, completing an apprenticeship, and retiring from service are commonly marked by a formal acknowledgment of the duties being accepted or released.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
Serrovanian institutions depend on recorded responsibilities. Officials swear to the limits of their offices, guilds preserve the terms of their charters, and households keep accounts of debts, inheritances, and obligations. Public scribes and witnesses are familiar figures in markets and village squares.

Formal challenge gives disputes an accepted shape. The grievance, the contest, and the consequences are declared before witnesses. Some challenges involve arms; others test skill, testimony, or the ability to substantiate a claim. Violence within accepted terms can be lawful. Breaking those terms threatens the trust that made the challenge possible.

This order has its cruelties. Wealth buys patient advocates, old records can preserve old injustices, and a precisely worded agreement can conceal an ugly intention. Serrovanians argue fiercely over whether justice lies in honoring the record or correcting what should never have been written into it.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text:
Serrovanians follow many faiths, but promises, testimony, and remembrance occupy an honored place across them. Shrines often witness marriages, reconciliations, and vows of service. An ancestor may be remembered through an obligation their descendants continue to uphold.

Mercy also has a recognized dignity. Publicly releasing someone from an oath can be an act of generosity remembered as long as the oath itself.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
• Keep your word when doing so becomes inconvenient.
• State your terms before the contest begins.
• Stand witness when another needs the truth recorded.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
• Knowingly swear an oath you intend to break.
• Falsify a record entrusted to your care.
• Inflict punishment beyond the terms of an accepted challenge.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Many Serrovanian surnames take the form of a short promise: something a household declares it will uphold. These names are inherited, and families take particular pride in living up to them. Someone named Speaktrue can expect a lie to be remembered with unusual clarity.

People commonly retain given names from their family or ancestry. The surnames below are familiar Common translations of Serrovine names.

Common given names Cerran, Dovra, Ilyra, Maroven, Orven, Selka, Tavren, Veyra.

Common surnames Bearwitness, Holdfaith, Keepword, Speaktrue, Standfast.

Example names Cerran Keepword, Dovra Standfast, Ilyra Speaktrue, Maroven Bearwitness, Selka Holdfaith.

lore.label: Summary
lore.text: Reachers thrive where people and possibilities meet, building livelihoods through sharp observation, useful introductions, and bargains worth making again.

lore.label: About
lore.text:
Kestrel Reach spreads across a wide river delta, where channels divide around crowded islands and trade-towns rise above the floodwater. Six languages may be spoken along a single dock, with three more heard by evening. Boats bring unfamiliar goods, travelers bring unfamiliar customs, and someone is always looking for a person who understands both.

Reachers grow accustomed to difference early. An elven shipwright, a dwarven grain factor, and a human ferryman may share a neighborhood, a business venture, and a running argument about harbor fees. Local knowledge means knowing how people prefer to be approached, which courtesies matter to them, and whom they trust to make an introduction. A good broker can accomplish with an afternoon’s conversation what an armed company might spend a season making worse.

lore.label: If you want...
lore.text: If you want a character who is comfortable among unfamiliar faces, always listening for an opportunity, and rarely without someone they could ask for help, choose Kestrel Reach.

lore.label: You Might...
lore.text:
Learn a few useful words whenever you encounter a new language.
Introduce yourself by naming someone the other person already knows.
Look for what each side needs before deciding that a dispute cannot be settled.

lore.label: Others Probably...
lore.text:
Expect you to know a useful contact in almost any port.
Wonder whether your friendly questions are leading toward a proposal.
Rely on you to notice the custom, omission, or hidden cost they overlooked.

lore.label: Dress and Bearing
lore.text:
Reach clothing reflects crowded docks, changeable weather, and goods arriving from distant places. Practical layers, secure pockets, broad hats, and garments kept clear of ropes are common. Fabrics and ornaments travel freely between communities, adapted to each wearer’s build and family traditions.

Reachers often display a token of their trade, vessel, or trading house where an acquaintance can recognize it. Greeting gestures vary between neighborhoods, and knowing which one to offer can make a warmer introduction than expensive clothes.

lore.label: Upbringing and Milestones
lore.text:
Young Reachers learn by carrying messages, helping with household business, and accompanying experienced relatives through markets and landing places. They are taught to notice who has spoken, who has been overlooked, and whether everyone understands the same terms.

A first independently completed bargain or entrusted journey often marks growing responsibility. Its importance lies in returning with the agreement fulfilled and the other party willing to deal with the household again. These milestones follow readiness and circumstance across the Reach’s many ancestries.

lore.label: Society
lore.text:
The delta depends on cooperation that extends beyond individual towns. Ferrymen need maintained channels, merchants need dependable warehouses, and everyone needs the flood banks to hold. Neighborhood associations, trading houses, craft guilds, and harbor officials overlap in a web of favors and competing responsibilities.

Reputation moves quickly along the waterways. A generous settlement can bring business from three towns away; a cheated customer can arrive ahead of you wherever you hoped to trade next. Brokers earn their standing by remembering details, protecting confidences, and finding terms that people will actually honor.

The Reach’s friendliness can conceal hard boundaries. Established houses sometimes keep profitable routes among themselves, and an introduction may matter more than an excellent offer. Reachers admire people who open opportunities for others, but they also know how easily a well-connected few can decide who gets a place at the table.

lore.label: Beliefs
lore.text:
Reach shrines welcome travelers, returning crews, and families whose traditions came from elsewhere. River spirits, ancestral patrons, and gods of craft, fortune, and safe passage all receive offerings.

Many Reachers regard hospitality as an obligation that travels. Someone shelters a stranger today because another household may shelter their own kin tomorrow. Gifts, favors, and acts of kindness create relationships whose value cannot always be entered into an account.

lore.label: Popular Edicts
lore.text:
Learn how to greet people on their own terms.
Give the other party a reason to trade with you again.
Share a useful introduction when it costs you little.

lore.label: Popular Anathemas
lore.text:
Abuse the protection offered to a guest.
Conceal a danger that makes an agreement impossible to fulfill.
Betray a confidence entrusted to you as a broker.

lore.label: Names
lore.text:
Reach surnames often come from waterways and shoreline features. A name may remember the bank where a household built its first home, the channel its boats worked, or the landing from which its members scattered across the world. Families carry these names inland long after the river itself has become a distant memory.

Given names mingle freely across languages and ancestries. The surnames below are commonly used in their Common forms.

nodes.name: Cover the Angle ❶↺
nodes.effect:
You gain the Cover the Angle ❶↺ Reaction:
Requirements You are wielding a rigid object like a weapon or a shield.
Trigger An adjacent ally is being Attacked by a foe that is no more than one size larger than you with a melee weapon.

The attack roll is measured against your Guard instead of your ally’s Defense, and any Bind that forms is with your weapon or shield.

nodes.name: Larger than Life
nodes.effect:
Requirements You are wearing Plate in all Zones.

You're treated as one size larger for the purposes of affecting other creatures with Disarm, Grapple, Reposition, Shove, and Trip. Similarly, you're treated as one size larger for the purposes of creatures affecting you with those same maneuvers, as well as with Swallow Whole and similar actions.

nodes.name: Parry ❶↺
nodes.effect:
You gain the Parry ❶↺ Reaction:
Requirements You are wielding a rigid object like a weapon or a shield.
Trigger Your foe is no more than one size larger than you, and is Striking you with a melee weapon.

You gain a +2 Situation bonus to Guard against the triggering attack. If the Strike is a Graze or a Miss, you may immediately attempt to Gain Control of the attacking weapon.

nodes.name: Riposte
nodes.effect: After you successfully Parry, instead of Controlling the attacking weapon, you may at once make a Quick Strike against its owner.

Endure.meta: Defense constellation • Might (survive what does come through)
Endure.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Endure Training
nodes.effect:
You are Trained in Endure. Endure answers Blasts and Blights (see Chapter 4: Threats and Permitted Defenses).

You reduce your Load Strain by 1 (to a minimum of 0) at Trained, 2 at Expert, 3 at Master, and 4 at Legendary.

nodes.name: Shrug It Off
nodes.effect: Reduce each instance of Persistent Damage you take by your Might. This can never reduce it below 1.

nodes.name: Second Wind ❷
nodes.effect: Once per day, dig deep: regain Vigor equal to half your level plus your Might.

nodes.name: Braced Frame
nodes.effect: You gain a +2 Situation bonus to Guard against Shove, Trip, and Reposition.

nodes.name: Blade Brake ❶↺
nodes.effect:
Requirements You are wielding a rigid object like a weapon or a shield.
Trigger You would be moved by a forced movement effect.

You plow your weapon into a floor, wall, or another sturdy surface, anchoring yourself in place. If you would be moved 6 feet or more, you are moved only 1 foot. Otherwise, you don’t move at all.

Lore.meta: Skill constellation • Wits (the template every Lore (X) Constellation copies)
Lore.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Deep Knowledge
nodes.effect: You are Trained in this Lore: add the Constellation's rank to its checks. Recall and research within its field; you know its history, texts, and secrets.

nodes.name: Practical Application
nodes.effect: +2 Situation to any check where you can explain how this field directly applies. The GM is the judge; the story is the proof.

nodes.name: Well Read ⓿
nodes.effect: Once per scene, Recall Knowledge ⓿ about your field.

Elementalism.meta: Magic • Wits (Manipulation of fire, cold, water, wind, lightning, and related natural energies. Defenses and rituals are expressed as elemental alterations, not generic spells.)
Elementalism.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Elementalism Training
nodes.effect: Elemental Dart (Blow, Zoned, 30 ft): Quick ❷ deals 1d6 fire or cold; Focused ❸ deals Damage Dice d6; Committed ❹ adds a 2-foot push or pull to a Hit, as described by the chosen element. Damage type is fixed when casting.

effects.committed: Damage Dice d6; on a Hit, a 2-foot push or pull as the chosen element describes

Flamecraft.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Flamecraft Training
nodes.effect: Flame Seed ❷/❸/❹: cast a fire attack; on a Focused Hit, one creature takes Damage Dice d6 fire (Pervasive). Committed can instead affect a tiny 2-foot-radius area at reduced dice, subject to playtest.

effects.focused: On a Hit, one creature takes Damage Dice d6 fire
effects.committed: A tiny 2-foot-radius area at reduced dice, subject to playtest

nodes.name: Lingering Flame
nodes.effect: On a Flamecraft Committed Hit, you may ignite one unoccupied 1-foot square in the effect until your next Opportunity; this terrain deals 1 fire damage to a creature entering it (once per creature).

Stormcraft.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Stormcraft Training
nodes.effect: Static Lash ❷/❸/❹: a Zoned lightning Blow against one target, 1d6 / Damage Dice d6 electricity; Committed can push the target 2 feet on a Hit.

effects.committed: Damage Dice d6 electricity; on a Hit, push the target 2 feet

nodes.name: Stormsense
nodes.effect: You can identify an approaching natural storm and detect nearby exposed electrical currents or active storm magic; GM decides meaningful range.

Forceweaving.meta: Magic • Might (Control of momentum, kinetic pressure, gravity, impact, and physically manifest barriers. Emphasizes tactical displacement and interposition.)
Forceweaving.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Forceweaving Training
nodes.effect: Kinetic Dart (Blow, Zoned, 30 ft): Quick ❷ deals 1d6 bludgeoning; Focused ❸ deals Damage Dice d6; Committed ❹ may push a creature 2 feet on a Hit instead of gaining extra damage.

effects.committed: On a Hit, push a creature 2 feet instead of gaining extra damage

Kinetics.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Kinetics Training
nodes.effect: Vector Shove ❷: Blast versus Evade or Endure. On a Hit, push a creature up to 3 feet; on a Graze, 1 foot; on a Critical Hit, 5 feet. No damage.

effects.quick: On a Hit, push a creature up to 3 feet; on a Graze, 1 foot; on a Critical Hit, 5 feet. No damage.

nodes.name: Anchor Point
nodes.effect: ❶↺ When you would be pushed by a Blast, gain +2 Endure against it; on Graze or Miss, prevent its forced movement.

Barriers.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Barriers Training
nodes.effect: Interpose Force ❶↺: When you or an adjacent creature suffers damage from a Zoned attack, reduce that damage by 2 after applicable Protection; once per round.

nodes.name: Woven Wall
nodes.effect: ❸ Prepared: create a short, stationary force barrier that grants Lesser Cover until your next Opportunity; exact dimensions require playtest.

Vitalism.meta: Magic • Might (Magic of living systems: restoration, growth, poison, disease, tissue, and decay. Healing and blight are different applications of one domain.)
Vitalism.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Vitalism Training
nodes.effect: Sapping Touch (Blight, Pervasive, adjacent): Quick ❷ deals 1d4 poison; Focused ❸ deals Damage Dice d4 poison; Committed ❹ reduces the target’s next Move by 1 foot on a Hit. Creatures immune to poison ignore its damage.

effects.committed: On a Hit, the target's next Move is reduced by 1 foot

Restoration.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Restoration Training
nodes.effect: Read Injury ❶: Identify whether a visible injury is a Wound, fatigue, poison, or ordinary loss of Vigor, subject to observable limits.

nodes.name: Restorative Practice
nodes.effect: Healing of Vigor or Wounds is reserved for a dedicated balance pass. At-will healing must not invalidate Spent, Wounds, recovery, or Downtime.

Decay.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Decay Training
nodes.effect: Toxic Bloom ❸: Prepare a small area of Blight; on a Hit, creatures in it take Damage Dice d4 poison damage (Pervasive). The initial area size is intentionally limited for testing.

effects.focused: On a Hit, creatures in the area take Damage Dice d4 poison

nodes.name: Purge Toxin
nodes.effect: ❶: Suppress one poison-induced penalty affecting yourself until the end of your next Opportunity; does not remove damage or end the poison.

Mindweaving.meta: Magic • Wits (Influence over perception, thought, emotion, dreams, memory, and illusions. Its illusions can mislead but do not create physical barriers.)
Mindweaving.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Mindweaving Training
nodes.effect: Mind Needle (Beguilement, Pervasive, 20 ft): Quick ❷ deals 1d4 psychic; Focused ❸ deals Damage Dice d4 psychic; Committed ❹ can instead make the target Wrong-Footed to your next attack on a Hit. The target answers with Awareness or Guard.

effects.committed: On a Hit, the target is instead Wrong-Footed to your next attack

Illusion.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Illusion Training
nodes.effect: False Image ❷: Create one stationary image in a visible 2-foot space until your next Opportunity. It cannot cause damage or physically impede movement.

nodes.name: Veiled Gesture
nodes.effect: When casting an Illusion spell, you may conceal obvious visual signs from distant observers; nearby creatures still perceive ordinary speaking and movement.

Emotions.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Emotions Training
nodes.effect: Unsettle ❷: Beguilement against Awareness or Guard; on a Hit, the target is Frightened 1; Graze and Miss have no effect.

effects.quick: On a Hit, the target is Frightened 1; Graze and Miss have no effect

nodes.name: Steady Thoughts
nodes.effect: ❶↺ When you would become Frightened, reduce the incoming Frightened value by 1 (minimum 0); once per round.

Spiritcraft.meta: Magic • Presence (Manipulation of souls, spiritual bindings, oaths, curses, and unseen presences. Spiritcraft has its own defensive practices and rites.)
Spiritcraft.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Spiritcraft Training
nodes.effect: Spirit Lash (Blow, Zoned, 20 ft): Quick ❷ deals 1d6 force; Focused ❸ deals Damage Dice d6 force; Committed ❹ can suppress a spirit’s movement by 2 feet on a Hit. This spell may interact with incorporeal targets as specifically allowed by its Trait.

effects.committed: On a Hit, suppress a spirit's movement by 2 feet

Oaths.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Oaths Training
nodes.effect: Mark the Promise ❶: Witness a willing spoken promise and recognize whether its terms have been repeated or deliberately misquoted; this does not compel honesty.

nodes.name: Binding Vow
nodes.effect: ❸ Prepared ritual: Consecrate a spoken oath between willing participants. Spiritual consequences require separate agreed narrative or scenario rules.

Exorcism.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Exorcism Training
nodes.effect: Sense Presence ❶: Detect whether a manifested spirit is nearby, but not its exact square unless otherwise Observed.

nodes.name: Break Possession
nodes.effect: ❹ Prepared Beguilement against a possessing spirit’s Guard or Awareness; on a Hit, it must release the host until its next Opportunity. Cannot be repeatedly applied to the same spirit within one round.

effects.committed: On a Hit, the possessing spirit must release the host until its next Opportunity

nodes.name: Acrobatics Training
nodes.effect: You are Trained in this skill: add the Constellation's rank to its checks.

nodes.name: Tumbling Retreat ❶
nodes.effect: Step your full Speed away from your foes. You still cannot Step in Difficult Terrain or Greater Difficult Terrain.

nodes.name: Slip the Grasp
nodes.effect: +2 Situation bonus to Escape.

nodes.name: Kip Up ❶
nodes.effect: Stand up. This movement doesn't trigger Reactions.

nodes.name: Kip Away
nodes.effect: When you Stand, you may Step as part of the same action.

nodes.name: Tumble Behind
nodes.effect: When you successfully Tumble Through, the foe whose space you passed through is Wrong-Footed against the next attack you make before the end of your next Opportunity.

nodes.name: Mobility
nodes.effect: When you Move half your Speed or less, that movement does not trigger Intercepts or other Reactions. You can use Mobility when Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Moving if you have the corresponding movement type.

nodes.name: Athletics Training
nodes.effect: You are Trained in this skill: add the Constellation's rank to its checks. Every talent here requires this.

nodes.name: Bull Rush ❷
nodes.effect:
Move, then Shove.
Add 1 foot to the push for every 2 feet you moved first.

nodes.name: Wrestler's Grip
nodes.effect: A creature you have Grabbed takes a −2 Situation penalty to Escape.

nodes.name: Titan Wrestler
nodes.effect: Grapple, Shove, and Trip creatures up to two sizes larger than you.

nodes.name: Diplomacy Training
nodes.effect: You are Trained in this skill: add the Constellation's rank to its checks. Every talent here requires this.

nodes.name: Rally ❶
nodes.effect:
You gain the Rally ❶ action:
Rally ❶
Auditory, Emotion, Mental
Roll Diplomacy against a Threshold of 14. On a success, one ally within 30 feet who can hear you gains a +1 Situation bonus to their next Defense roll before your next Opportunity. On a critical success, +2, and they can Recenter ❶ as a free action.

nodes.name: Talk Them Down ❶
nodes.effect:
You gain the Talk Them Down ❶ action:
Talk Them Down ❶
Auditory, Concentrate, Emotion, Mental
Roll Diplomacy against the target's Guard. On a success, it takes a -2 Situation penalty to Attacks against you until the end of the next round; on a critical success, until the end of the encounter. On a critical failure it gains a +1 Situation bonus to Attacks against you.

nodes.name: Coordinated Effort
nodes.effect: When you Aid an ally, the bonus is +2 instead of +1, and +3 on a critical success.

nodes.name: Command the Field ❷
nodes.effect:
You gain the Command the Field ❷ action:
Command the Field ❷
Auditory, Concentrate, Emotion, Mental
Roll Diplomacy against a Threshold of 14. On a Success, two allies who can hear you may each Step ⓿. On a critical success, they may each Move half their Speed instead.

nodes.name: Guile Training
nodes.effect: You are Trained in this skill: add the Constellation's rank to its checks. Every talent here requires this.

nodes.name: Feinting Step ❶
nodes.effect: Feint, then Step.

nodes.name: Sell the Feint
nodes.effect: When you critically succeed at a Feint, the target is off-guard to everyone, not just you, until the end of the next round.

nodes.name: Overextending Feint
nodes.effect: On a successful Feint, you can use the following success and critical success effects instead of any other effects that would occur when you Feint.Critical Success The target takes a -2 Situation penalty to all attack rolls against you before the end of the next round.Success The target takes a -2 Situation penalty to its next attack roll against you before the end of the next round.

nodes.name: Distracting Feint
nodes.effect: While a creature is Off-Guard or Wrong-Footed by your Feints, it also takes a -2 Situation penalty to Awareness and Agility checks and Thresholds.

nodes.name: Intimidation Training
nodes.effect: You are Trained in this skill: add the Constellation's rank to its checks. Every talent here requires this.

nodes.name: Battle Cry ⓿↺
nodes.effect:
Trigger You are about to roll Initiative.
Demoralize every enemy within 15 feet with a single roll, compared separately against each one's Guard.

nodes.name: No Quarter
nodes.effect: When you drop a creature, you may Demoralize ⓿ one enemy who saw it fall.

nodes.name: Unnerving
nodes.effect: A creature you have Demoralized this encounter takes a −1 Situation penalty to attacks against you for the rest of it.

nodes.name: Brutal Beating
nodes.effect: Whenever your Strike is a critical hit and deals damage, the target is Frightened 1.

nodes.name: Stealth Training
nodes.effect: You are Trained in this skill: add the Constellation's rank to its checks. Every talent here requires this.

nodes.name: Knife in the Dark
nodes.effect: When you Hit a creature that is Off-Guard or Wrong-Footed to you, you choose which Zone the blow lands on.

nodes.name: Lost in the Noise ❶↺
nodes.effect:
Trigger An attack against you Misses.
Effect If you have cover or concealment, Hide as part of this Reaction.

nodes.name: Killing Stillness
nodes.effect: The first time each encounter that you Strike a creature that is unaware of you, a Graze becomes a Hit.

nodes.name: Underhanded Assault ❷
nodes.effect: You Sneak up to a foe adjacent to one of your allies. You can roll against the foe you're Sneaking up on, even if it's currently observing you, as though you were hidden. You take a -2 penalty on your Stealth check. If your Stealth check against the chosen foe succeeds, you can make a melee Strike against that foe at the end of your Sneak, and they are Wrong-Footed against that Strike.

Melee.meta: Weapon • Might (Represents transferable fundamentals: measure, timing, reading an opponent, footwork, maintaining guard, committing to a strike, etc. Melee is a parent Constellation: every Talent you buy in Two-Weapon Fighting, Shield Fighting, Brawling, Dueling, Great Weapon Fighting, Spear & Polearm Fighting, or Armored Fighting counts toward your Melee rank.)
Melee.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Melee Training
nodes.effect:
You are Trained in Melee. Strikes and other Maneuvers involving melee weapons are usually Melee checks.

Special Intuitive weapons use your full Melee Proficiency Bonus. Practiced or Technical weapons do not; see Chapter 5: Equipment for rules on Weapon Traits.

You gain the Intercept ❶↺ Reaction:
Requirements You are wielding a melee weapon.
Trigger A foe moves from outside your Total Reach to inside it, or attempts to Strike you with an Unwieldy weapon from inside its Unwieldy distance.

Make a Quick Strike against them. If it is a Critical Hit, their action is interrupted.

nodes.name: Weapon Familiarity
nodes.effect: Choose a Weapon Group or a Technical weapon. You are Familiar with weapons in that group or that Technical weapon.

nodes.name: Quick Draw
nodes.effect: Use a Reaction ⓿↺ to draw or stow an item, weapon, or shield in each hand (or in both hands, if it requires two hands).

nodes.name: Turn the Weapon
nodes.effect: You may deal bludgeoning damage with any Familiar melee weapon you wield, striking with the pommel, the haft, or the flat. Its damage die drops one step when you do (d12 to d10 to d8 to d6 to d4).

nodes.name: Sure Grip
nodes.effect: +2 Situation bonus to your Guard against Disarm regarding a Familiar weapon. When a Disarm against you would succeed, you keep hold of the weapon and suffer only the loosened grip.

nodes.name: Read the Steel ❶
nodes.effect: Study one creature you can see. Until the end of the encounter you know the Protection and the material of each of its Zones, and your Strikes against it ignore 1 Protection.

nodes.name: Reactive Strike
nodes.effect: Your Intercept ❶↺ also triggers when an Observed creature within your Reach begins a Manipulate Maneuver, or a Motion Maneuver that would carry it out of your Reach. You may only use this with weapons in which you are at least Expert. On a Critical Hit, the triggering Maneuver is disrupted: it fails, and any actions still to come in it are lost.

nodes.name: Feeling
nodes.effect: You read the pressure in the bind before you commit to it. When your Gain Control Misses, the target does not take Control of your weapon; the Bind is simply neutral.

nodes.name: Winding
nodes.effect: While you Control a foe's weapon, your Committed Strike ❸ against that foe is not Weighted, and your Strikes against that foe do not end the Bind. You cut from the bind without leaving it.

nodes.name: Master Cut
nodes.effect: When you Counter, you gain a +2 Situation bonus to the Defense you roll against the triggering attack. Your parry and your cut are one motion.

Ranged.meta: Weapon • Agility (Represents what transfers between every weapon that leaves the hand: judging distance, timing a release, leading a moving target, and shooting past friends. Ranged is a parent Constellation: every Talent you buy in Archery, Crossbow Fighting, or Missile Skirmishing counts toward your Ranged rank.)
Ranged.sparks: Crit succeed or crit fail on any roll with consequences, directly related to a talent in this constellation.

nodes.name: Ranged Training
nodes.effect:
You are Trained in Ranged: add this Constellation's Proficiency Bonus to your attack rolls with any weapon that leaves your hand: bows, crossbows, slings, and thrown weapons (a dagger uses Melee in your hand and Ranged in the air).
Special Intuitive weapons use your full Ranged Proficiency Bonus. Practiced or Technical weapons do not; see Chapter 5: Equipment.

nodes.name: Aim ❶
nodes.effect: Concentrate Choose one creature you can Observe within your weapon's range. Your next ranged Strike against it before the end of your next Opportunity gains a +1 Situation bonus, and on a Hit you may choose the Zone it strikes.

nodes.name: Loose and Move
nodes.effect: After making a ranged Strike, you may Step ⓿ once per round.

nodes.name: Steady Release
nodes.effect: Your ranged Strikes ignore a target's Lesser Cover (the +1 it grants, and the Zone rule) if you have not Moved this round. Patience finds the gap.
